argument_map.gap: Authors state earlier work focused on NLR, lacked SIRI–FI evaluation, and had limited population generalizability; this is an attributed literature-gap claim, not a newly verified systematic review.
argument_map.gap_location: paper_extracted.txt L106–120; PDF p2 Background final paragraph; p8 Discussion
argument_map.question: In US NHANES 1999–2016 adults described as 50 and older, are CBC-derived inflammatory markers associated with concurrently measured FI-defined frailty?
argument_map.measurement: N/L, M/L, N*M/L, P*N/L → log continuous or marker quartiles as X; modified 36-item Rockwood FI → FI>0.3 as Y.
argument_map.estimation: Logistic models with two covariate sets → conditional odds ratios; RCS/subgroups/additional adjustment probe shape, heterogeneity and sensitivity.
argument_map.outputs: Fig1 defines sample; Table1 describes it; Table2 continuous-marker OR; Table3 marker-quartile OR; Fig2 RCS; Fig3 subgroup analysis; supplement S6/S7/FigS1 additional adjustment.
argument_map.conclusion_limit: Cross-sectional adjusted association under the chosen frailty definition. Causal effect, validated clinical threshold and future prediction performance are not established.

age_boundary.fact_inclusive: Abstract L29 and Background L120 say '50 and older'; Results L247–255 excludes participants younger than 50.
age_boundary.fact_exclusive_wording: Discussion Principal findings p6, L532–534 says 'aged over 50'.
age_boundary.decision: Use >=50 only as interpretation supported by eligibility wording, preserve >50 wording as unresolved textual inconsistency; no verified author code.
age_boundary.not_established: The age wording alone does not explain the sample-count discrepancy. Count at exactly age 50 was not examined in this audit.

sample_discrepancies.fact: Published sequential arithmetic: 92062-70392-2508-5503-152=13507; age step leaves21670.
sample_discrepancies.location: PDF p3 Results, paper_extracted.txt L247–256; previous audit Fig1 p4
sample_discrepancies.existing_candidate: 04-paper execution section reports public RIDAGEYR>=50 N=24119, FI complete N=9814, marker N=9786.
sample_discrepancies.judgment: Published arithmetic is internally consistent but raw-data selection is not reproduced. Different inclusion/missing rules, age boundary and reporting error remain candidates, not established causes. No count tuning.

sample_discrepancies.fact: 152 excluded for covariate missingness, yet Table1 retains627 missing drinking values.
sample_discrepancies.judgment: Do not infer universal complete-case analysis; model-specific N and missing-category/imputation policy unreported.

sample_discrepancies.fact: Table1 smoking yes7187 + no6308 =13495, twelve below total13507; subgroup yes5077+2110=7187, no4690+1618=6308.
sample_discrepancies.location: paper_extracted.txt L405–414; PDF p5 Table1; previous audit reports supplement smoking total13507
sample_discrepancies.judgment: Potential table discrepancy; cannot determine which number or coding is correct.

sample_discrepancies.fact: Published frail count3729/13507 is approximately27.61%, whereas Table1/Abstract report24%.
sample_discrepancies.judgment: Weights may explain count/percentage difference, but title/footnote conflict prevents treating this explanation as confirmed.

stages.title: Data row and research question
stages.original_claim: Participant-level cross-sectional NHANES1999–2016 data join CBC, frailty and covariates.
stages.why_needed: Connect literature gap to target population, X/Y and one-person row before calculations.
location: PDF p2 Background/Study population; text L106–144
not_reported: Author files, raw variable names, join keys/duplicate handling and code
stages.reuse: Existing one-person trace and variable map are teaching/candidate lineage only; verify against raw artifact before reuse. Not author-identical.

stages.title: CBC measurement
stages.original_claim: NLR=N/L; MLR=M/L; SIRI=N*M/L; SII=P*N/L from absolute cell counts.
stages.why_needed: Turn measured counts into interpretable exposures; distinguish accessible proxies from complete inflammation measurement.
location: PDF p2 Assessment of CBC-derived inflammatory biomarkers; p5 Table1 units
not_reported: Cycle-specific raw mappings, zero/invalid counts and repeated measurement handling
stages.reuse: Formula implementation reusable after unit and denominator checks; candidate distribution cannot establish author equivalence.

stages.title: Frailty measurement
stages.original_claim: Rockwood multidimensional deficit accumulation chosen;46 minus10 nutritional items gives36; criterion1/0; FI>.3 frail.
stages.why_needed: Define what Y measures before choosing binary outcome model; Fried and FI are distinct constructs.
location: PDF p2 Background/Frailty assessment; supplement S1 via previous audit; PDF p9 limitations
not_reported: Self-report thresholds and raw response codes
Exact FI denominator and partial-missing rules
Author-specific treatment of laboratory range boundaries
stages.reuse: operational36, complete36 sum/36 and coding sensitivity may be reused only as declared reconstruction choices. Prior reference22 68-item missing rule must not be imported as Han36 fact; reference23 does not resolve all thresholds.

stages.title: Eligibility and missingness
stages.original_claim: Cross-sectional; younger-than50 exclusion and CBC/FI/covariate exclusions reported.
stages.why_needed: Determine whom associations describe and how missingness changes sample composition.
location: PDF p3 Results L247–256; p4 Fig1 via previous audit; p6 L532–534; p9 limitations
not_reported: Operational definition of insufficient FI/CBC data
stages.reuse: Earlier24119/9814/9786 selection results are diagnostic candidates only. Require artifact/provenance validation; discrepancy remains open.

stages.title: Descriptive distributions/Table1
stages.original_claim: Medians/IQR and counts/percentages summarize sample; survey test footnotes appear.
stages.why_needed: Inspect distributions, imbalance and denominators before association models.
location: PDF p3 Statistical analysis; p5 Table1 title/footnotes, text L331–338
stages.reuse: Earlier descriptive figures usable as explicitly candidate sample output, never substituted for original Table1.

stages.title: Binary outcome and odds
stages.original_claim: Logistic regression estimates odds of FI>.3 with OR/95%CI.
stages.why_needed: Distinguish probability, odds, OR and continuous-FI change; choose estimator for Y.
location: PDF p2 Frailty assessment; p3 Statistical analysis; p6 Tables2–3
not_reported: Exact link implementation/package and inferential details
stages.reuse: OR teaching and candidate binary Model1 interpretation reusable; cross-sectional OR is not incidence risk or future prediction accuracy.

stages.title: Scale and model assumptions
stages.original_claim: Authors log-transform four markers citing nonnormality.
stages.why_needed: Define exposure contrast and check functional form; predictor normality is not logistic-regression requirement.
location: PDF p3 Statistical analysis; p6 Table2 footnote
not_reported: Functional-form diagnostics, influential cases, collinearity, separation checks
stages.reuse: Natural-log models are declared candidate choice; previous diagnostics do not validate author model or prove all assumptions.

stages.title: Adjustment/Table2
stages.why_needed: Ask whether association persists conditional on measured covariates; compare adjustment scope.
location: PDF p3 Covariate assessment and Statistical analysis; p6 Table2 footnote
not_reported: BMI25/PIR boundaries, references, model-specific N and survey regression setting
stages.reuse: Candidate Model1 and fractional mean model may illustrate different estimands; Model2 author reproduction remains unconfirmed. Outcome components overlap with diabetes/hypertension adjustment.

stages.title: Marker quartiles/Table3 versus classroom extension
stages.original_claim: Table3 uses quartiles of each inflammatory marker, lowest as reference; reports p-trend.
stages.why_needed: Express exposure comparison in groups; distinguish it from grouping FI and comparing marker means.
location: PDF p3 Statistical analysis; p6 Table3; supplemental S2–S5 via previous audit
not_reported: Weighted quantile algorithm, ties and unrounded cuts
Conflicting SIRI Q3 bound in main text
stages.reuse: Earlier FI-quartile Welch/ANOVA/KW results are course extension, not Table3 reproduction. Use frozen analysis_plan.json families24 pairs/4 omnibus/4 trend; old handoff six-pair recommendation is superseded.

stages.title: Shape, heterogeneity, robustness and conclusion
stages.original_claim: RCS investigates nonlinearity; subgroups and added-covariate sensitivity explore heterogeneity and stability.
stages.why_needed: Bound a single OR with evidence on shape, uncertainty and definition dependence.
location: PDF p3 Statistical analysis; p4 Results; pp7–8 Figs2–3; p9 limitations; supplement S6/S7/FigS1 via previous audit
not_reported: Multiplicity and exact subgroup interaction implementation
Resolution of text SIRI smoking versus Fig3c discrepancy
stages.reuse: Candidate threshold/platelet/fractional sensitivities and simulations are separate educational evidence. Neither confirms original spline nor clinical validation; original10-paper exposes published and candidate results.

reuse_gate: Reuse existing results only with source artifact, candidate definition, cohort, estimand, code/environment provenance and status label retained. This audit did not rerun or independently validate any prior numeric output.

log_base_source_check.location: PDF p5 Table1; paper_extracted.txt L495–515; PDF p3 methods and p6 Table2 note
log_base_source_check.fact: Table1 presents unlogged marker values, not paired logged marker values: total NLR2.14, MLR0.29, SIRI1.17, SII496; fit2.08/0.29/1.13/486; frail2.35/0.31/1.33/531.
log_base_source_check.judgment: These values cannot identify the log base. Original text only says logarithmically transformed. Any ln/log10 coefficient rescaling is mathematical sensitivity, not evidence of author implementation.
log_base_source_check.additional_note: p3 Results text describes2.08/0.29/1.13/481.85 and quartile cutoffs, whereas Table1 total values differ. We do not resolve this reporting difference by choosing a log base.
